comparison: Perfect alignment on simulation results (C52-C61) comparing polygenic score construction methods. Both evaluations support these findings without challenge, with peer reviewers accepting the demonstration of the polygenic amplification model's promise.

Perfect alignment on the core conceptual argument about polygenic GxE (C7-C8, C18, C35-C36, C63-C64). Both evaluations strongly support this central thesis, with peer reviewers explicitly praising the demonstration of greater statistical power under polygenic GxE assumptions.

Strong alignment on UK Biobank empirical findings (C6, C23, C30-C34). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative results and validation approach, while peer reviewers accept these findings as valid evidence for the bias-variance tradeoff framework without challenge.

Strong alignment on background and motivation claims (C1-C2, C11-C17). Both evaluations treat these as well-supported by literature and accepted knowledge in the field, establishing the foundation for the study.

Strong alignment on theoretical framework and mathematical derivation (C3-C5, C20-C22). OpenEval emphasizes detailed mathematical derivations, while peer reviewers praise the mathematical precision and clarity. Peer review also includes C62 (main theoretical conclusion) which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Good alignment on claims about limitations of single-variant approaches and polygenic architecture (C9-C10, C19, C39). Both support these claims, though OpenEval also includes C40-C41 which peer reviewers evaluate separately.

Partial alignment on Pallares et al. reanalysis. OpenEval covers full simulation study (C42-C51), while peer review focuses on the demonstration that amplification model explains patterns (C37-C38, C47-C51). Both accept the reanalysis as valid evidence for the amplification model's plausibility.

Partial overlap on amplification model mechanism (C37-C38). OpenEval evaluates these claims separately as describing prior work and mechanistic explanation, while peer reviewers group them with the Pallares reanalysis as part of demonstrating the amplification model's plausibility.

Minimal overlap on C62 (main theoretical conclusion). OpenEval evaluates this claim separately as a summary conclusion, while peer reviewers include it with the broader theoretical framework evaluation alongside C3-C5, C20-C22.

Minimal overlap on technical mathematical details (C24, C26, C29). OpenEval groups these with the full theoretical framework, while peer reviewers evaluate them separately as supporting the bias-variance framework, implicitly accepting them through endorsement of the overall theoretical contribution.

Minimal overlap on specific background claims (C11-C12). OpenEval includes these in a broader background evaluation (C1-C2, C11-C17), while peer reviewers evaluate C11-C12 separately, accepting the framing about model organisms versus human genetics.

Minimal overlap on theoretical predictions about cumulative effects (C40-C41). OpenEval groups these with broader claims about polygenic architecture, while peer reviewers evaluate them separately as part of the endorsed polygenic GxE framework.
